market_holds: Spot 11.85-11.90 (Yahoo bars, 2026-11-18 intraday; sealed baseline 11.90), -10% over 5 sessions and +6% over 20; -22% from the 52w high. No usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided, OI 181), so there is no implied move; the sealed expected move is the 5.35% median historical reaction. Re-timing the prior prints off Yahoo daily bars: the FY25 Q4 print with the first FY26 guide went +28% (11/19/2025 to 11/20 close), Q1 about +5%, Q2 about +6-9%, Q3 (8/5/2026 amc) -7.5% when EBITDA guidance was cut to the low end of $380-410M with FCF $90-110M held. Coverage is thin: 1-2 analysts, Hold, targets $15-16 (Wells Fargo raised to $16 on 2026-07-15; investing.com shows one Hold). Quarter consensus EPS ~$0.40 and revenue ~$899-919M on aggregators (no reliable dates). There is no visible FY27 EBITDA consensus. Guide arithmetic: FY26 low end $380M minus YTD $282M gives an implied Q4 of ~$98M, against $90M in Q4 FY25; FCF needs ~$58-78M in Q4 after ~$32M YTD. The stock trades inversely to oil, and the price already reflects the macro: it fell to 10.62 on 10/15 with Brent ~$126, then rose +6.6% on 11/4 (Brent -14%) and +5.5% on 11/9 (Brent -7%). Since 11/11 it has fallen ~10% while Brent was flat and IWM fell ~4.5%. RSU-vest Form 4s on 11/4 and 11/14-17 only; no open-market insider trades.
view: The reaction will turn on the FY27 guide (EBITDA and the free cash flow it implies), not the quarter. Two forces I can document pull opposite ways and I cannot tell which one the street has wrong. Bullish: FY26 carried ~$80M of integration cost and ~$60M of capex, the CFO said the end of the transition reduces one-time cash costs, and ~$20M of synergy and CORE run-rate carries into FY27. A large FCF guide on a ~$425M equity cap could produce the same 'FCF yield' headline that drove +28% a year ago. Price/cost has been favorable even through the spring resin spike: Americas had +$11M price-cost spread in Q3 while the plastics resin PPI rose 17% Mar-May. Resin then fell back and has been flat Jul-Sep, so Q4 Americas should not be squeezed. Bearish: European energy has blown out since the August call. EU gas averaged ~$15.5/MMBtu in fiscal Q3 against ~$21.4 in fiscal Q4 (Jul $17.9, Aug $20.9, Sep $25.5), and TTF is €85-100/MWh in Oct-Nov against roughly €30-35 a year ago. Brent spiked to $135 on 10/2, so Q1 FY27 resin rises again. Rest of World (Europe plus Latin America) was already -7% in Q3, and management named European softness and geopolitical cost pushes. The analyst numbers are likely stale (last dated actions July and possibly 8 Oct), so a cautious FY27 EBITDA guide that bakes in European energy could land below them. The market has traded this macro day by day through oil, so neither the FCF roll-off (which management flagged) nor the energy shock (front-page news) is clearly unpriced. Net: a slight negative lean on the EBITDA guide risk, well inside coin-flip territory. No recommendation.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the European energy hit in the FY27 EBITDA guide against stale, thin estimates. I could not quantify Magnera's European energy exposure, hedging or surcharges, and the stock already swings with oil, so I cannot show it is unpriced.

recommendation.reason: The line is the FY27 guide. One documented tailwind (integration cash costs rolling off, synergy carryover, favorable price-cost) and one documented headwind (European gas roughly 2.5-3x a year ago, an October oil spike) pull opposite ways. The price already tracks the oil and energy macro daily, and there is no FY27 consensus to measure a surprise against. I cannot name a mechanism that the price clearly lacks, so I make no call.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A FY27 free cash flow guide well above ~$130M with EBITDA held near or above $400M would make this a clear up-move. FY27 EBITDA guided below FY26's ~$380M, citing European energy, would make it a clear down-move.

self_critique: The negative lean rests on macro data everyone can see, and the stock has already moved on it. Management could also guide FY27 with energy surcharges and synergies offsetting it, and lead with a large FCF number, as last November. The equity is only ~20% of EV, so a modest beat on FCF could gap it up 10%+. The stock has also already fallen 10% into the print with small caps, which lowers the bar. The bear case is that a 'dynamic macro' cautious guide from a company that already cut to the low end once in August fits the pattern of the one negative reaction.
approach_notes: Reading the freshest physical series myself (FRED EU gas, Brent, resin PPI) and re-timing the past reactions off the tape paid off most. The baseline history mis-dates the amc prints. P4 ('priced in is a claim to prove') cut both ways here: the macro is visibly priced through the oil correlation, but the guide size cannot be shown either way without a FY27 consensus, and that gap is what kept this at no call.
